text: uses model.matrix trick produce numeric matrix containing numeric dummy variables, can used calculating correlations plotting heatmaps dendrograms. First, assessing three variables. code: logLik(fit.pois) ## 'log Lik.' -730.0133 (df=5) logLik(fit.negbin) ## 'log Lik.' -147.1277 (df=6) logLik(fit.ZIpois) ## 'log Lik.' -303.0276 (df=6) logLik(fit.ZInegbin) ## 'log Lik.' -146.7677 (df=7) listoffits <-   list(     pois = fit.pois,     negbin = fit.negbin,     ZIpois = fit.ZIpois,     ZInegbin = fit.ZInegbin   ) lapply(listoffits, logLik) ## $pois ## 'log Lik.' -730.0133 (df=5) ##  ## $negbin ## 'log Lik.' -147.1277 (df=6) ##  ## $ZIpois ## 'log Lik.' -303.0276 (df=6) ##  ## $ZInegbin ## 'log Lik.' -146.7677 (df=7) qchisq(0.95, df = 1) ## [1] 3.841459 qchisq(0.95, df = 2) ## [1] 5.991465

what: Create residual deviance plots using the functions defined in the lecture.
title: Session 5 lab exercise: loglinear regression part 2
text: (base graphics) functions defined create first two panels residuals plots types models. Let’s make plots. shortcut, remember list models? ’m going use explicit loop time instead lapply can use vector names plot titles. Although saw evidence chi-square test Negative Binomial distribution fit better Poisson distribution (surprising since data -dispersed), diagnostic plots show Negative Binomial distribution still fit well . take interpretation coefficients models plenty skepticism. dataset tricky ’m sure offhand good model fit . Note, line par(mfrow=c(1, 2)) works base graphics (ggplot2), creates 1 row 2 column plot panel.
code: plotpanel1 <- function(fit, ...) {   plot(     x = predict(fit),     y = residuals(fit, type = "pearson"),     xlab = "Predicted Values",     ylab = "Pearson Residuals",     ...   )   abline(h = 0, lty = 3)   lines(lowess(x = predict(fit), y = resid(fit, type = "pearson")),         col = "red") } plotpanel2 <- function(fit, ...) {   resids <- scale(residuals(fit, type = "pearson"))   qqnorm(resids, ylab = "Std Pearson resid.", ...)   qqline(resids) } par(mfrow=c(1, 2)) for (i in seq_along(listoffits)){   plotpanel1(listoffits[[i]], main = names(listoffits)[i])   plotpanel2(listoffits[[i]], main = names(listoffits)[i]) }
